In a brushed DC motor, the part that turns the shaft is the

Rule: the rotor (armature) carries the coil and turns the shaft.
Apply: the stator stays fixed and makes the magnetic field.
Check: the brushes only feed the current, and they do not turn.
The commutator of a brushed motor
reverses the coil current each half turn

Rule: the commutator swaps the coil connection to the brushes.
Apply: the swap keeps the force pushing in the same turning direction.
Check: the field comes from the stator, not from the commutator.
A wire with current in a magnetic field feels a force that is
at right angles to both the field and the current

Rule: F = I × B, so the force is normal to the plane of I and B.
Apply: this force on the coil sides gives the torque.
Check: a force along the wire or the field does not turn the rotor.
A PM motor has T_stall = 2 N·m and ω_NL = 3000 rpm. The speed at maximum power is

Rule: the maximum power of a PM motor is at half the no-load speed.
Apply: 3000 / 2 = 1500 rpm.
Check: 3000 rpm is the no-load speed, 750 rpm is a quarter of it and 2000 rpm is not a half.
The brushes of a motor are usually made of

Rule: brushes are graphite contacts that slide on the commutator.
Apply: graphite conducts and wears gently, so it protects the commutator.
Check: plastic does not conduct and iron would wear the commutator.
The stator of a brushed motor makes the field with

Rule: the stator provides the fixed magnetic field.
Apply: it uses permanent magnets or electromagnets.
Check: the brushes, the commutator and the shaft are not field sources.
Which brushed motor is used for an elevator?

Rule: a series motor gives a very large torque at low speed.
Apply: an elevator needs this torque to lift a heavy load.
Check: a shunt motor suits a constant-speed load such as a fan.
Which brushed motor keeps an almost constant speed when the load changes?

Rule: in a shunt motor the field is in parallel with the armature.
Apply: the field stays constant, so the speed varies little with the load.
Check: a series motor changes its speed strongly with the load.
The most widely used AC motor is the

Rule: the induction motor is efficient, cheap and needs little maintenance.
Apply: its rotor gets its power by induction, so it needs no brushes.
Check: the other motors are less common in AC drives.
In an AC induction motor the rotor gets its power by

Rule: the rotating stator field induces current in the rotor.
Apply: no brushes or commutator are needed.
Check: this is why the induction motor needs little maintenance.
The three windings of a three-phase generator are spaced

Rule: three equal phases share 360°, so each is 360° / 3 = 120° from the next.
Apply: this spacing makes a smoothly rotating field.
Check: 90°, 180° and 60° do not divide 360° into three equal parts.
A 60 Hz three-phase supply has phases whose peaks are separated in time by

Rule: delay = T / 3.
Apply: T = 1 / 60 = 16.67 ms, so the delay is 5.56 ms.
Check: 16.67 ms is the full period and 8.33 ms is half of it.
AC induction motors are by nature
machines that must not carry a load

Rule: the speed changes little over a wide load range.
Apply: the torque-speed curve is almost flat in speed.
Check: induction motors work under load and need no brushes.
Above the pull-out torque, the torque of an induction motor

Rule: the pull-out torque is the peak of the torque-speed curve.
Apply: beyond it, the torque falls and the motor slows or stalls.
Check: no real motor gives an infinite torque.
A series motor must not start with no load because
its speed would rise out of control
it would overheat the brushes only

Rule: with no load nothing limits the speed.
Apply: in the series motor the speed rises out of control and can damage it.
Check: the motor does turn, and the main danger is the runaway speed.
